null : current)); if (result.ok) { announce(`Background: ${choice.name}.`); return; } — announce not guarded by the same currency check, and checked = failed ? \"none\" : (picked ?? requested) re-reads the old requested once picked is cleared","suggested_fix":"Announce only when the choice is still current (use the functional setPicked result or compare against a ref), and keep checked optimistic until the snapshot's state.effect matches the request (e.g., clear picked only when choiceOfEffect(state.effect)?.id === choice.id or on failure)."},{"severity":"SUGGESTION","file":"apps/web/src/presentation/guest-meeting/devices/device-field.tsx","line":88,"claim":"Locking the select by preventDefault on mousedown does not stop the native picker on touch devices (iOS/Android fire the picker from touch, not mousedown), so a 'locked' (pre-permission) picker opens and shows the placeholder option on mobile, contrary to the documented 'it ignores changes and does not open' behavior.","evidence":"onMouseDown={(event) => { if (locked) event.preventDefault(); }} — no touchstart/click guard","suggested_fix":"Also preventDefault on touchstart/click (or pointerdown) when locked, or render the locked state as a non-select control that keeps the same accessible name/description so nothing opens."}]}

Let me analyze this diff carefully. It's a React 19 web meeting app on LiveKit. The packet covers devices, lobby preview, levels, background UI, enable-audio prompt. Let me go through each file and look for real defects. 1. `background-asset-paths.ts` — root-relative paths for mediapipe wasm and model. In a Tauri host, root-relative might resolve differently (tauri://localhost or http://tauri.localhost). The comment says same bundle resolves against their own origin. Probably fine. But if the app is deployed under a subpath, root-relative breaks — speculation. Not necessarily a defect. 2. `lazy-realtime-room.ts`: - `idleSnapshot` includes `audioPlayback: "allowed"` — fine. - `catalog.subscribe` — subscribes at module/factory creation. But there's no unsubscribe; page lifetime, so fine. - One issue: `setMediaEnabled: (kind, enabled) => real?.setMediaEnabled(kind, enabled) ?? notJoined()`. If `real` exists, fine. If not, returns connection-lost. OK. - `getSnapshot: () => real?.getSnapshot() ?? idle` — but the idle snapshot's `support` is computed with `options.backgroundEffects ?? false`, and `loadLiveKitRoom` passes `backgroundEffects: true`. The comment says "composeMeeting passes the matching `backgroundEffects: true` to the lazy room; the two must agree." So there's an implicit contract; if they don't agree, support flips when media loads. That's a comment-documented constraint; the load file comment says the two must agree. But is composeMeeting actually shown? No — it's in another packet presumably. Can't verify. However there's a subtle bug: `detectConferencingSupport` is called eagerly at `createLazyRealtimeRoom` — that's SDK-free, fine. - Bug candidate: In `adopt`, listeners/consent listeners are subscribed to the real room; but the `idle` snapshot may differ from real room's initial snapshot, and subscribers are notified? Actually adopt doesn't notify listeners — presumably `connect` triggers a snapshot change and notify elsewhere. Not shown. Skip. - Bug: `disconnect` doesn't reset `real` to null. After disconnect, `getSnapshot` returns real room's snapshot — that's fine since it's connected=false presumably. - Bug: `refreshDevices: () => real?.refreshDevices() ?? catalog.refresh()`. Return types must match — presumably both return Promise>. Fine. - Race: `catalog.subscribe(() => { if (real !== null) return; ... })` — after adoption, real reports devices itself. OK. 3. `load-livekit-room.ts` — fine. 4. `device-copy.ts` — fine, copy strings. `switchFailed` uses `DeviceError` — fine. 5. `device-field.tsx`: - The `locked` mode: `aria-disabled` but not actually `disabled`, and it prevents default on keys and mousedown. But it keeps `onChange` guard. One issue: keyboard users can still Tab to it and... it blocks ArrowUp/Down etc. but the select remains focusable — that's the intent (per docs). However, `onTouchStart` isn't guarded — on touch devices, tapping opens the picker? Actually `onMouseDown` preventDefault usually prevents opening the dropdown on desktop; on mobile, the select opens on touch/click events, not mousedown necessarily. Mobile browsers synthesize mousedown before opening? Actually preventing mousedown default does prevent the dropdown from opening on many browsers, but on iOS Safari, the picker opens on touchend; preventDefault on mousedown may not stop it. So on iOS a locked select might open with "Default microphone" placeholder. That's a minor a11y/behavior concern. Hmm. But `onChange` guard prevents changes. Also with a single option shown ("Default microphone" placeholder), picking it does nothing. Not really harmful. - `value={listed ? value : ""}` with options being either real options or a single empty-value option. Fine. - Note: `className="has-[select[aria-disabled=true]]:opacity-50"` — opacity-50 reduces contrast? It's on the select itself, not text contrast per se — opacity 50% halves contrast of the label text. For a disabled/locked control that's common; disabled controls are exempt from contrast requirements in WCAG. OK. 6. `device-options.ts`: - `optionLabel`: strips "Default - " prefix. For default device with empty label → "System default". Fine. - `deviceOptions` positions — labels "Microphone 1" for unlabeled devices. - `hasDevicePermission`: labels non-empty. Fine. - `shownDeviceId`: falls back to default. Fine. - `listedDeviceId`: fine. 7. `level-meter.tsx`: - `
